title: Scroll-linked reveal with reduced-motion fallback
description: Content sections that ease into view as they enter the viewport (short opacity and translate change), implemented with CSS scroll-driven animations where supported and IntersectionObserver otherwise. Content is visible by default; the animation is an enhancement and is removed entirely under reduced motion.
intent: Add a sense of sequence to a long marketing or story page without hiding content or making anyone wait.
characteristics: visible-by-default content; animation only adds polish
runs once per element, never on scroll back
prefers-reduced-motion: no transform, content simply present
transform and opacity only, no layout properties
interaction: Triggered by scroll position only; never delays links or form controls; no scroll hijacking or snapping.
responsive: Same behavior at all sizes; reduce distance on small screens; skip entirely for content above the fold on load.
accessibility: Content must never stay invisible if JavaScript fails or the observer never fires; honor prefers-reduced-motion; avoid animating text that users are trying to read (WCAG 2.3.3 for interaction-triggered motion).
limitations: Scroll-driven CSS animations are not available in every browser; the observer fallback is required.
On dense app screens this adds noise; use it on narrative pages only.
